best_for: Database administrators and developers on Windows who manage SQL Server or Azure SQL and need full admin tools, not just a query editor.
description:
SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) is Microsoft's all-in-one tool for working with databases that run on the Microsoft SQL Database Engine. Besides SQL Server and Azure SQL Database, that covers Azure SQL Managed Instance, SQL Server on Azure virtual machines and SQL databases in Microsoft Fabric.

You browse and manage tables, users and other objects in Object Explorer, write and run scripts in the Query Editor, and read execution plans to see why a query is slow. A preview tool suggests query hints you can apply. You can also configure Integration Services, Analysis Services and Reporting Services at the server level; building packages, models or reports is done in SQL Server Data Tools instead.

points.title: Free, even at work
points.text: Microsoft says SSMS is free for personal or enterprise use and needs no Visual Studio subscription. It is closed source and has its own license terms.

points.title: Windows only
points.text: There is no macOS or Linux version. SSMS 22 needs 64-bit Windows 11 or Windows Server 2019, 2022 or 2025, and runs natively on Arm64. Windows in S mode and LTSC editions are not supported.

points.title: It installs through Visual Studio Installer
points.text: The download is a small stub that opens Visual Studio Installer; there is no standalone MSI. You need admin rights, at least 4 GB of RAM, and 4 GB to 50 GB of disk depending on the parts you add.

points.title: What is new in 22
points.text: It is now 64-bit and based on Visual Studio 2026, with a first dark theme, Git integration and JSON output in the results grid. GitHub Copilot can be added as an optional component, but is not installed by default.

points.title: Older servers need older SSMS
points.text: SSMS 22 works with SQL Server 2014 and later plus Azure SQL. For older servers, or the legacy SSIS service of an earlier release, keep an older SSMS; it installs side by side with versions 16 through 21.

points.title: No third-party extensions
points.text: Microsoft does not support third-party extensions and closes feedback about them without looking.

points.title: 28 versions kept
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 28 versions of SSMS 22, all machine-wide x64 installers.
